body:
I BROKE #2009 WITH MY OWN REBASE AND I AM FIXING IT. Reporting before it is
finished rather than after, because the cause is a check I skipped.

#2009's BASE IS NOT MAIN. It is `task-1289-work` — #2009 is STACKED on #1972.

    #2009  head bug-1420-work  base task-1289-work
    every other open PR        base main

I rebased BOTH branches onto main independently. They share four commits, so
each replayed the same four separately and produced different shas for identical
content. Result: bug-1420-work went 4 behind its own base and merge-tree against
it CONFLICTS, while merge-tree against MAIN is clean. That is why GitHub said
CONFLICTING while git said fine — I was checking the wrong base, and so was my
rebase script.

WHAT I NEARLY REPORTED INSTEAD: "#2009 shows CONFLICTING but git says clean, so
the API is stale." I had already written that sentence. GitHub was right and I
was measuring against a base the PR does not use.

THE FIX, in progress: rebuild bug-1420-work as task-1289-work + its ONE unique
commit.

    origin/task-1289-work @ c2d996334b
    + cherry-pick d718d10862  "match GitHub Actions bash strictness"
    = dcbf13970b, 1 commit ahead of its base, cherry-pick clean
    --check ok, zero markers, full suite running now

I verified d718d10862 is the only commit unique to it — the other four match
task-1289-work's by subject and content.

SCOPE CHECK, because the first question is whether I did this to others: NO. I
enumerated every open PR's base and #2009 is the ONLY one not targeting main. So
the damage is one PR and it is the one I am repairing.

THE LESSON IS CHEAP AND I HAVE ADOPTED IT: read the PR's BASE before rebasing
onto main. My script hardcoded origin/main for all six. Five were right by
luck — they happened to target main — and the sixth was wrong for a reason the
script could not see because it never asked.

SEPARATELY: #1972's verdict landed — Build GREEN at 10m36s, "first real CI result
since the BUG-1526 mask lifted", all three findings standing verbatim. Pure
rebase, zero rework, as expected. That phrase is the clearest confirmation yet
that the gate was masking real signal.
subject: I broke #2009: it is STACKED on #1972 and I rebased both onto main independently — fixing now; no other PR is stacked
